status.note: Local integration and documentation are complete on the exact integrated source; the public merge, immutable tag, image build and digest remain pending until actually performed.

changes.summary: Flash-Next DFlash2 launch profile and setup candidate: separate incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2 draft, FR-Spec 65,536-ID map, resident rowwise-FP8 output head reuse, 0.95 memory fraction for image-workload headroom, 6 requests / 36 Mamba slots, 524,288-token context, 2,048-token draft window, HiCache/NIXL unchanged; becomes the default profile for new setups.

Verify width is routed per active batch size by the bundled fixed policy (block 6 at one running request, block 4 at two or more) instead of acceptance-driven adaptation; proposal-probability scratch is keyed by width and routing stays valid when a width captures nothing. Concurrency routing, not acceptance-based tuning; the 3.0-era SPECULATIVE_NUM_DRAFT_TOKENS setting is refused on this profile.

Remove the preset KV-token cap; the engine sizes the shared pool from profiled memory inside the static memory fraction. An explicit MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS remains a deliberate positive, page-aligned override on every profile.
FR-Spec candidate projection for DFlash2 narrows the draft's searched vocabulary while the target keeps full verification.
Support the resident rowwise FP8 output head in DFlash2 so the draft reuses the target's converted head.
Bound draft GPU KV allocation to sliding-window requirements.
Preserve ordinary host HiCache capacity while the draft GPU pool stays bounded.

Remove the incorrect tp_size > 1 rejection from DFlash2 capture; ordinary TP2 already produces complete replicated hyper-connection state at the capture point. TP2 is expected to work; it has not been tested on two-GPU hardware.
Drop finished requests from the running batch before every admission and count a request's held req_to_token row once at admission.
Honor stop-regex matches inside accepted speculative blocks on both DFlash2 block sizes.
Prevent the identified scheduler crash when token-probability requests mix with ordinary generation.
Retain the measured .97 memory fraction for the native MTP FR-Spec recipe, separate from the DFlash2 .95 default.
Native NEXTN MTP Flash-Next profiles remain launchable with unchanged recipes but are deprecated: no further updates or testing.

Agreed subset: QSA restore ordering, packed scratch initialization, shared Chat/Responses chat_template trust gate, absent tool-call fields, stream timestamps, malformed-image 400s, collection before KV sizing, existing ignore_eos accounting, freed-response-state handling.
Optional Swift FP8 PLE transplant/verification recipe with whole-data-section, table-width, scale and payload validation; serving qualification remains contributor-owned.

settings.flash_next_dflash2_width_routing: block 6 at one running request; block 4 at two or more
settings.kv_pool: automatic on every profile; explicit MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS remains available

performance.presentation_detail: Real five-slide workflow on final source a60f442 at C1 W6: 121 model turns matched 121 server requests, 1,676 complete decode intervals over 909.385 s, 192,349 server output tokens including reasoning, prompt growth 42,637 to 253,267 tokens; total workflow time including tools and rendering was 33 minutes 25 seconds.
performance.conditions: Native elapsed-weighted complete active-decode intervals and sampled peak from the same window, including reasoning; normal non-greedy sampling. Rows keep their recorded source/configuration labels: 5ca3f39 for the FR-Spec fixed-W4 normal/full-C6 and W6 coding-flow screens, earlier 27f9eaa for the W4 reasoning and 27B fixed-W8 screens, and a60f442 for the presentation. C4/C6 rows are aggregate over the full running batch, not per-request rates. The corrected full-batch means supersede the earlier drain-inclusive 522.69/386.26 summaries. The internal synthetic code-edit width screen is intentionally not published.
performance.hardware_note: All local numbers are one RTX PRO 6000 at TP1; TP2 is expected to work and has not been tested on two-GPU hardware.
